body:
`hkb serve` is scoped to one repo, because everything downstream of `ctx` is. `repoRoot()` is `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from the cwd (`src/board.js:109`), and `fetchBoard` queries that owner/repo plus a single `kb:board:<slug>` label (`src/tasks.js:88`). `--board` picks among boards *within* a repo; there is no cross-repo view and no way to ask for one.

So the moment you run hkb on a second repository, the cost is: a second `hkb serve --port 4667` (both default to 4666, `src/serve.js:23`), a second browser tab, and remembering which is which. Nothing is broken — the port clash even fails cleanly, naming the fix (`src/serve.js:407`) — it is just friction that scales linearly with adoption, which the fourth value now says is a gap to close rather than a workflow to document.

**Scope: the read side only.** One server, several boards, one page. The dispatcher has the same one-loop-per-repo shape and is the more valuable fix, but it carries a real question this card does not — how `max_in_progress` and the daily spawn cap account across boards — so it stays a separate card.

**What has to change.** `serve` currently closes over a single `ctx`; the work is to make it hold several and route every per-board read through the right one:

- **Board selection.** Needs a source for "which checkouts". A `--repos <path,path>` flag is the smallest thing that works; a user-level list (this spans repos, so it cannot live in any one `.kanban/`) is the better ending. Do not scan the filesystem for `.kanban/board.json` — surprising, slow, and it will find abandoned trials.
- **Per-board local state.** `dispatcherState(ctx.root)` (`src/serve.js:107`), `logPathFor(ctx.root, …)` and the log-tail endpoints (`src/serve.js:306,371`) all resolve against one root. Each needs to resolve against the board the request names, so the page can show which boards have a live dispatcher and tail the right log.
- **The page.** `web/index.html` is one inline file, no build step — keep it that way. The seven columns (`COLUMNS`, `src/serve.js:21`) stay; boards become a grouping *within* them, or a switcher. Whichever, a card must show which repo it belongs to, because #12 on two boards is two different tasks.
- **Drag-and-drop.** The board runs real verbs. Every one must target the board the card came from — a card dragged in the wrong board's context would run a verb against the wrong repo. This is the part to test hardest.

**Frugality.** One GraphQL query per board per poll, unchanged — N boards is N queries, on the same conditional-read/304 path that exists now. No new dependency, no build step. `gh` auth is already global, so one token reads them all.

**Verify.** Two checkouts, one `hkb serve`, both boards on one page; a dispatcher running for one and not the other is visible per board; tailing a log from each reaches the right file; a verb run by drag-drop lands on the right repo — assert this against a fake, not by eye. The single-repo invocation must keep working exactly as it does today with no flags.
title: One serve, every board: two repos should not cost two servers, two ports and two tabs
